scenario: Today’s generative track asks the same question: how generative recommendation can still be computable, credible, and usable under production constraints. One line of work first gets the long-input, wide-beam inference pipeline right, rather than rushing to write a custom kernel. Multimodal Semantic ID diffusion has to ask whether a modality actually narrows the candidates still in the catalog. A flow-network objective written for an online setting cannot be copied onto offline logs, and preference optimization can be hacked on unsampled items. Long histories have to be compressed into an interest sketch first, and automatically evolving a recommender needs feedback that points to the failure and the next change. Medication combinations put safety constraints into inference itself, and medical concepts write hierarchy into the identifier. Whether generation is usable increasingly depends on whether those constraints are written into the generation process.

papers.title: Optimize the Cob, Then the Kernel: Optimizing Beam Search for Generative Recommendation Inference
papers.authors: Shing Wai Pun, Kai Wu, Pengfei Xia, Hui Zang, Wei Guo, Yong Liu
papers.summary: Generative recommendation inference is unlike ordinary language-model serving: inputs are long, beam search is wide, and only a few output tokens are produced. Existing engines often treat each beam as an independent sequence in a batch, so the shared prompt prefix is reread from the KV cache, and each generation step is a separate engine call, with host-side beam work and runtime cache-block management sitting between steps. This approach concatenates beams along the sequence dimension with Tree Attention to remove those repeated KV reads. It also adds precomputed partial-attention masks, a static KV cache, graph compilation, operator fusion, and vocabulary-constrained decoding. Without custom kernels, end-to-end latency on Ascend NPUs falls by up to 25× relative to vLLM, and generation latency is comparable to a strong baseline that does use custom kernels. ==The generation pipeline should be optimized as a whole before anyone reaches for a custom kernel.==
papers.abstract: Generative recommendation (GR) inference differs substantially from conventional LLM serving, featuring long input sequences, wide beam search, and only a few fixed output tokens. Existing LLM serving engines such as vLLM process beams as batched independent sequences, causing redundant KV cache accesses over the shared prompt prefix. Furthermore, vLLM executes each beam search generation step as a separate engine invocation, incurring host-side beam processing overhead between decoding steps and substantial runtime KV block management in PagedAttention. Using Tree Attention, we concatenate beams along the sequence dimension to eliminate redundant KV accesses, and further optimize execution through pre-generated partial-attention masks, static KV cache allocation, loop-unrolled generation dispatch, TorchAir graph compilation, automatic operator fusion, and vocabulary-constrained decoding. Without the use of custom kernels, our approach reduces end-to-end latency by up to 25x over vLLM
papers.score_note: 针对生成式推荐推理（长输入、宽 beam、短固定输出）优化 Tree Attention 与静态 KV，相对 vLLM 端到端延迟最高约 25x，且无需自定义 kernel。生成式赛道核心，不放到 infra 以免跨赛道重复。

papers.title: CONCORD-Rec: Catalog-Conditioned Modality Utility for Semantic-ID Diffusion Recommendation
papers.authors: Haopeng Jin, Bingkang Shi, Tao Yu, Yifei Ma, Hao Liu, Hongzhu Yi, Jinwen Luo
papers.summary: In multimodal generative recommendation with discrete Semantic IDs, a historical image or text does not always reduce ambiguity in the catalog; sometimes it only changes token predictions. When a modality is missing, degraded, or in conflict with another, uniform fusion can also carry misleading content into iterative denoising. One method supervises a modality gate with counterfactual catalog-partition utility. On the same feasible catalog and a partially masked Semantic ID, it compares the loss on the target group with and without a modality, then allocates bounded modality corrections by position and availability, while keeping a behavior-only prediction as fallback. On MicroLens-100K, NDCG@20 rises 4.00% over uniform fusion in the clean setting, and 7.95% when 30% of modalities are missing. ==Whether a modality helps depends on whether it narrows the candidates still in play.==
papers.abstract: Multimodal generative recommendation with discrete semantic identifiers (SIDs) requires distinguishing historical modalities that merely alter token predictions from those that genuinely reduce catalog-level ambiguity. When audiovisual, visual, or textual streams are missing, degraded, or semantically conflicting, uniform fusion and unconstrained token gates can propagate misleading content across iterative denoising steps. We propose CONCORD-Rec, a reliability-conditioned discrete diffusion recommender supervised by counterfactual catalog-partition utility. Given a fixed tokenizer and a partially masked SID state, CONCORD-Rec evaluates out-of-fold teacher coalitions over the exact feasible catalog support and aggregates item posteriors across the target code partition at each unresolved position. Rather than distilling raw token probabilities directly, the resulting counterfactual loss differences supervise an availability-masked tokenwise gate that allocates bounded modality residual

papers.title: Improving LLM-Based Recommenders with Conservative Generative Flow Networks
papers.authors: Xuan Yu, Feng Niu, Rui Zhu, Yudong Zhang, Xu Wang, Yang Wang
papers.summary: Generative flow networks have been used to raise diversity and ease popularity bias in LLM-based recommendation, but most of their objectives were written under online-style assumptions. Offline recommendation can learn only from a fixed logged dataset, so token transitions cover only the prefixes that dataset supports. Applying a sub-trajectory balance objective as if the setting were online becomes non-identifiable, and probability mass can be assigned to regions the data never supports. The paper formalizes this failure and names three sources that drive the learned policy away from the policy implied by the data: flow overestimation, forward mass leakage, and backward compensation. A conservative objective then explicitly penalizes unsupported forward flow and learns the policy under dataset constraints. ==An offline recommender cannot borrow an online flow-network objective unchanged.==
papers.abstract: Generative Flow Networks (GFlowNets) have recently been used to improve diversity and mitigate popularity bias in LLM-based recommender systems, yet most objectives are developed under online-style assumptions. In offline LLM-based recommendation, learning is constrained to a fixed logged dataset, yielding partial support over token transitions on the dataset-induced token-prefix DAG. Naively applying Sub-Trajectory Balance (SubTB) becomes non-identifiable and can arbitrarily allocate probability mass to unsupported regions. We formalize this failure and identify three sources of non-identifiability that induce distributional shift between the dataset-implied policy and the learned policy: (i) flow overestimation, (ii) forward mass leakage, and (iii) backward compensation. To address it, we propose CFlower, which introduces a conservative SubTB objective that explicitly penalizes unsupported forward flow mass, and combines it with dataset-constrained policy learning with on-policy samp
papers.score_note: 用 Conservative GFlowNets 改进离线 LLM 推荐的多样性与流行度偏差，并形式化 SubTB 在离线设定下的不可辨识问题。

papers.title: Mitigating Reward Hacking in LLM-based Recommendation: A Preference Optimization Approach
papers.authors: Heyu Chen, Junkang Wu, Guoqing Hu, Kexin Huang, Xiang Wang, Jiancan Wu
papers.summary: When large language models are adapted for recommendation, preference methods such as DPO sharpen pairwise discrimination, but they remain open to reward hacking: the model exploits flaws in the reward signal, training metrics rise, and genuine recommendation quality does not. From a gradient view, pairwise updates barely move the ordering between a positive item and unsampled negatives, creating an insensitive region. Under the Bradley-Terry model, such regions can occupy a substantial share of the preference space, and rankings inevitably drift, because the model never really learns to separate a positive from negatives that never appeared in a pair. The method introduces pseudo-negatives and uses simulated preference optimization to restrain this kind of hacking, so updates can also reach rankings that were almost untouched before. ==Pairwise preference alone does not adequately constrain how unsampled items are ranked.==
papers.abstract:
Post-training adaptation has become the central paradigm for leveraging large language models (LLMs) in recommendation. 
While recent preference optimization methods, such as Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), enhance pairwise preference discrimination, they remain vulnerable to \emph{reward hacking}: models exploit imperfections in reward signals, leading to inflated training metrics without genuine recommendation gains.
We analyze this issue from a gradient perspective and formalize the concept of the 
\emph{$\varepsilon$-insensitive region}, where pairwise updates exert little influence on the ordering between positives and unsampled negatives.
Under the Bradley–Terry model, we further show that these regions can occupy a substantial fraction of the preference space, inevitably leading to misaligned rankings.

papers.title: Token-Efficient Long-Term Interest Sketching and Internalized Reasoning for LLM-based Recommendation
papers.authors: Zhihao Ding, Jinming Li, Shuai Mu, Jieming Shi
papers.summary: Using a language model to reason about user preference in recommendation runs into two practical problems. Histories are often long and noisy, sometimes spanning hundreds of items, and truncation throws away signals needed for long-term interest. In a decoder-only model, chain-of-thought also has to emit rationale tokens one by one, which makes inference latency hard to accept in production. One framework works on both sides at once. It does not prompt the raw history as a whole. It encodes and clusters item descriptions into a compact, token-bounded interest sketch that keeps persistent preferences and suppresses noise, so the model can still see long-term interest inside a limited token budget. It also internalizes the reasoning so rationale tokens need not be generated at every request. Recommendation reasoning then need not swallow the whole noisy history, nor pay the cost of writing a long rationale for every score. ==Long-term interest has to be compressed first, and the reasoning need not be written out every time.==
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can solve complex real-world tasks when prompted to generate chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning, motivating their use for preference reasoning in recommender systems. However, applying LLM reasoning on recommendation faces  two practical challenges. First, LLMs struggle to reason over long, noisy user histories that often span hundreds of items while truncation discards signals needed to capture long-term interests. Second, in decoder-only architectures, CoT requires generating rationale tokens autoregressively, leading to prohibitive inference latency for real-world deployment. To address the challenges, we propose SIREN, a framework that enables effective LLM-based rating prediction via long-term interest sketching and internalized reasoning. papers.title: Self-EvolveRec: Self-Evolving Recommender Systems with LLM-based Directional Feedback
papers.authors: Sein Kim, Sangwu Park, HongSeok Kang, Wonjoong Kim, Jimin Seo, Yeonjun In, Kanghoon Yoon, Hyunsik Jeon, Chanyoung Park
papers.summary: Automatic design of recommenders is often boxed in by a human-defined operator space when it uses neural architecture search, so innovation can happen only among predefined operators. Recent language-model code evolution moves into an open program space, but it still leans on scalar scores such as NDCG or hit rate, which do not say where the model failed or which way to change it. One framework adds directional feedback: a user simulator supplies qualitative critiques, a diagnosis tool checks the model quantitatively from the inside, and the diagnosis criteria evolve with the recommender architecture, so the evaluation ruler does not stay frozen on an old design. Starting from SASRec on the CDs dataset, NDCG@5 rises from 0.3559 to 0.3865, above DeepEvolve from the same seed at 0.3610. ==Automatically revising a recommender needs feedback that points to the failure and the next change, not only a score.==
papers.abstract: Traditional methods for automating recommender system design, such as Neural Architecture Search (NAS), are often constrained by a fixed search space defined by human priors, limiting innovation to pre-defined operators. While recent LLM-driven code evolution frameworks shift fixed search space target to open-ended program spaces, they primarily rely on scalar metrics (e.g., NDCG, Hit Ratio) that fail to provide qualitative insights into model failures or directional guidance for improvement. To address this, we propose Self-EvolveRec, a novel framework that establishes a directional feedback loop by integrating a User Simulator for qualitative critiques and a Model Diagnosis Tool for quantitative internal verification. Furthermore, we introduce a Diagnosis Tool - Model Co-Evolution strategy to ensure that evaluation criteria dynamically adapt as the recommendation architecture evolves. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Self-EvolveRec significantly outperforms state-of-the-art NAS
papers.score_note: Self-EvolveRec：用 LLM 方向性反馈做自进化推荐。

papers.title: Steering Diffusion Models Towards Credible Content Recommendation
papers.authors: Zhuo Cai, Shoujin Wang, Jin Li, Peilin Zhou, Victor W. Chu, Fang Chen, Tianqing Zhu, Charu C. Aggarwal
papers.summary: Diffusion models have entered recommender systems because they can capture complex distributions of item content and user behavior, and their recommendation accuracy is often strong. Existing methods, though, often chase accuracy alone and do not ask whether the recommended content is credible, so they may generate untrustworthy content such as fake news or misinformation, with real social cost. One method tries to steer diffusion toward more credible content recommendation. It rewrites the diffusion objective so generation is encouraged when conditioned on preference-related signals and discouraged when conditioned on untrustworthy content, and it uses a disentangled diffusion process to lessen the influence of that content on generation while aiming to keep recommendation accuracy. ==Content recommendation cannot be judged by accuracy alone; what is generated has to be credible as well.==
papers.abstract: In recent years, diffusion models (DMs) have achieved remarkable success in recommender systems (RSs), owing to their strong capacity to model the complex distributions of item content and user behaviors. Despite their effectiveness, existing methods pose the danger of generating uncredible content recommendations (e.g., fake news, misinformation) that may significantly harm social well-being, as they primarily emphasize recommendation accuracy while neglecting the credibility of the recommended content. To address this issue, in this paper, we propose Disco, a novel method to steer diffusion models towards credible content recommendation. Specifically, we design a novel disentangled diffusion model to mitigate the harmful influence of uncredible content on the generation process while preserving high recommendation accuracy. papers.title: RxDiff: Discrete Diffusion for Medication Recommendation with Inference-Time Safety Control
papers.authors: Jinke Feng, Wenjie Du, Xuchang Zhong, Yang Wang
papers.summary: Medication recommendation has to produce drug combinations that are effective and that keep harmful drug-drug interactions low. The difficulty lies in the combinatorics of a prescription: drugs affect one another and cannot be treated as independent labels to be scored one by one. Discriminative methods often predict each drug on its own and miss those dependencies. Autoregressive methods introduce sequential dependence, but they impose an arbitrary generation order and accumulate errors. Both mostly penalize interactions at training time, and have limited ability to regulate them for an individual prescription at inference. This work recasts medication recommendation as discrete diffusion: iterative denoising can revise choices in both directions, and an interaction-aware adjustment at each inference step lets safety constraints be enforced while the prescription is being formed, not only in the training loss. ==Safety constraints on a drug combination should be enforceable during inference, not only during training.==
papers.abstract:
Medication recommendation requires generating drug combinations that are therapeutically effective while minimizing harmful drug-drug interactions (DDIs). Both objectives are rooted in the combinatorial nature of prescriptions. Existing discriminative methods predict drugs independently, neglecting inter-drug dependencies; autoregressive methods introduce sequential dependencies but impose arbitrary generation orders and accumulate errors. Both paradigms confine DDI mitigation to training-time penalties, offering limited capacity to regulate interactions during inference for individual prescriptions. We reformulate medication recommendation as a discrete diffusion process and propose RxDiff, which leverages iterative denoising for bidirectional and revisable generation and provides a natural interface for dynamic DDI regulation at each step. papers.score_note: RxDiff：用药组合的离散扩散推荐，领域特殊。

papers.title: SMI: Ontology-Grounded Semantic IDs for Hierarchy-Aware Medical Concept Representation
papers.authors: Ziyang Song, Lia Shen, YIXUAN LI, Qincheng Lu, Weihao Li, Haoran Xu, He Zhu, Xinyu Wang, Yue Li
papers.summary: Biomedical language models give strong representations for clinical tasks, but they often miss the hierarchy among medical concepts, and the problem is sharper for rare, fine-grained clinical codes, because a hierarchy-agnostic vector becomes less informative as a concept gets rarer. A training-free method defines each diagnosis, procedure, or medication concept’s Semantic ID as the coarse-to-fine path through an expert ontology, then aggregates frozen biomedical embeddings across those levels so coarse clinical meaning can support a fine-grained code. The base version aggregates levels uniformly, and a variant can select level weights on validation data. On medication recommendation in MIMIC-IV, the level-weighted variant reaches an AUPRC of 77.6%, an F-score of 65.3%, and a Jaccard score of 50.5%, significantly better than the strongest baseline. ==Once hierarchy is written into the identifier itself, rare concepts can borrow meaning from the levels above them.==
papers.abstract: Biomedical language models (LMs) provide strong representations for clinical tasks, but they often fail to capture the hierarchical structure among medical concepts. This limitation is especially pronounced for rare and fine-grained clinical codes in long-tailed vocabularies, where hierarchy-agnostic LM representations become less informative as concept frequency decreases. We introduce Semantic Medical Identifier (SMI), a training-free framework for constructing ontology-grounded Semantic IDs and hierarchy-aware medical concept representations. For each diagnosis, procedure, or medication concept, SMI defines its Semantic ID as the coarse-to-fine path through an expert-defined medical ontology. SMI then aggregates frozen biomedical LM embeddings across the corresponding ontology levels to form hierarchy-aware medical concept representations that preserve coarse-to-fine clinical semantics.
